questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution makes it clear that Directive Principles of State Policy are fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the state to apply these principles in making laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 37**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Article 37 of the Indian Constitution states** that the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are fundamental to the governance of the country and that the state is responsible for applying them when making laws
 
• The **DPSPs are fundamental to the governance of the country,** and the state is responsible for applying them when making laws
 
• The DPSPs **are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law.**
 
• However, they are still essential to the governance of the country.
 
• The DPSP is** given in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 40**

 
 
• **​**This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) and states that the government should establish village panchayats as self-government units. 
 
 
 
• **Article 44**
 
 
• **​**This article is part of the Arbitration chapter of the ICSID and states that arbitration proceedings should be conducted under the Arbitration Rules and the provisions of the Section. 
 
 
 
• **Article 46**
 
 
• **​**This article is part of the DPSP and states that the government should promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections of society,
 
 
• particularly the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• The government should also protect these groups from exploitation and social injustice

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is also known as the ‘100 drums festival’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wangala.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Wangala Festival** is a traditional festival in the northeastern Indian state of Meghalaya that is also known as the "100 Drum Festival.
 
• The **Wangala Festival is a major festival** for the Garo Tribe.
 
• It's a convergence of multiple festivals on a single stage that takes place in the first week of November.
 
• The **festival lasts from two days to a week.**
 
• During the festival, **tribesmen make sacrifices to please their god Saljong.**
 
• The festival was first celebrated in December 1976 and has since gained popularity, attracting hundreds of tourists each year.
 
• The** festival is held in Asanang in West Garo **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Cheiraoba:**

 
 
• Cheiraoba is the traditional New Year festival of the Meitei community in the Indian state of Manipur.
 
• It is celebrated in April.
 
• The festival symbolizes the end of the old year and the beginning of a new one. 
 
 
 
• **Sanken**:
 
 
• Sanken, is the **New Year festival of the Khamti, Singpho, and**
 
 
• **other Theravada Buddhist communities** of **Arunachal Pradesh** and parts of **Assam**.
 
 
 
• It is celebrated in April and is marked by the ritual of bathing Buddha statues with water as a sign of purification and washing away sins.
 
 
 
• **Saga Dawa**:
 
 
• **Saga Dawa** is one of the most significant religious festivals for **Tibetan Buddhists** and is widely celebrated in the Himalayan regions,
 
 
• including **Sikkim** and **Ladakh**.
 
 
 
• It falls on the full moon day of the fourth month in the Tibetan lunar calendar, usually in **May or June**.
 
• The festival commemorates three important events in Buddha’s life: his birth, enlightenment, and death (parinirvana).

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Complete Adventures of Feluda’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyajit Ray**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyajit Ray, an iconic Indian filmmaker and write**r, created the character Feluda, a detective whose stories are set in India

 
 
• and are beloved by readers for their wit, intelligence, and engaging mystery plots.
 
 
 
• He is **often compared to Sherlock Holmes**, with his keen observational skills and analytical mind.
 
• **Feluda** is a fictional Bengali detective introduced by Satyajit Ray in 1965.
 
• He first appeared in the story **“Feludar Goyendagiri”** published in the children’s magazine **Sandesh**, which Ray edited.
 
• The stories are usually narrated by Feluda's cousin, **Topshe**, who plays the role of Watson-like companion.
 
• **The Complete Adventures of Feluda"** is a collection that brings together all of Feluda’s stories, spanning multiple volumes.
 
• The stories cover a wide range of mysteries, from murders to thefts and missing persons, often set against the backdrop of Indian cities, towns, and historical locations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mrinal Sen**

 
 
• He is one of the pioneers of Indian parallel cinema, known for making films that address social issues, political struggles, and the lives of the marginalized.
 
• His films, such as **"Bhuvan Shome" (1969)** and **"Mrigayaa" (1976)**,
 
 
• reflect the harsh realities of Indian society and deal with topics like class conflict and urbanization.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Ritwik Ghatak**
 
 
• Ritwik Ghatak’s films are marked by their intense emotional depth and cultural context.
 
• His work often drew from his own experience of the **Partition of Bengal**, which profoundly impacted him.
 
• Films like **"Meghe Dhaka Tara" (1960)** and **"Subarnarekha" (1965)** depict the trauma and displacement faced by refugees and marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Goutam Ghose**
 
 
• He is known for his work both as a documentarian and a feature filmmaker.
 
• His films often straddle the line between fiction and reality, reflecting deep empathy for rural life and the common people.
 
• Films like **"Padma Nadir Majhi" (1993)** and **"Moner Manush" (2010)** depict the struggles and resilience of ordinary individuals in the face of hardship.

questions.question: Which triangular plateau region of India lies south of the river Narmada?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Deccan plateau**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
 
• The Deccan Plateau in southern India is located between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats.
 
• It is the peninsular region between these ranges that is south of the Narmada river.
 
• To the north, it is bounded by the Satpura and Vindhya Ranges.
 
• The rivers which flow through the Deccan Plateau have created many deep valleys and have further subdivided the large Deccan Plateau into several smaller plateaus which include the Maharashtra Plateau, the Karnataka Plateau and the Andhra Pradesh / Telangana Plateau

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afdc90d1cd6c330fe652227291b95654ecc8817ed304f2e00e321d8fff1080da.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Baghelkhand is a region and also a mountain range in central India that covers the northeastern regions of Madhya Pradesh and a small area of southeastern Uttar Pradesh.

 
 
• Baghelkhand was known as Dahlia.
 
 
 
• The Malwa Plateau is bounded by the Madhya Bharat Plateau and Bundelkhand Upland to the north, the Vindhya Range to the east and south, and the Gujarat Plains to the west.
 
 
• The plateau is located in western Madhya Pradesh and south-eastern Rajasthan with Gujarat in the west.
 
 
 
• Marwar plateau is a region of western Rajasthan state in North Western India.
 
 
• It lies partly in the Thar Desert.

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan rulers was the first, who tried to convey his messages to his subjects concerning the idea and practice of dhamma through inscriptions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Mauryan ruler who first tried to convey his messages** to his subjects concerning the idea and practice of **dhamma** through inscriptions was **Ashoka**.
 
• Ashoka, after the Kalinga War, embraced Buddhism and used inscriptions, 
 
 
• known as the **Edicts of Ashoka**, to promote dhamma, which included ethical and moral teachings.
 
 
 
• The empire that Ashoka ruled was founded by his grandfather, Chandragupta Maurya, more than 2300 years ago.
 
• Chandragupta was supported by a wise man named Chanakya or Kautilya. Many of Chanakya’s ideas were written down in a book called the Arthashastra.
 
• He was the first ruler who tried to take his message to the people through inscriptions.
 
• Most of Ashoka’s inscriptions were in Prakrit and were written in the Brahmi script__.
 
• Kalinga is the ancient name of coastal Orissa.
 
• Ashoka fought a war to conquer Kalinga. However, he was so horrified when he saw the violence and bloodshed that he decided not to fight any more wars.
 
• He is the only king in the history of the world who gave up conquest after winning a war.
 
• Ashoka’s dhamma did not involve the worship of a god or the performance of a sacrifice.
 __
 
• He felt that just as a father tries to teach his children, he had a duty to instruct his subjects.
 
• He was also inspired by the teachings of the Buddha.
 
• He appointed officials, known as the dhamma mahamatta who went from place to place teaching people about dhamma.
 
• Ashoka got his messages inscribed on rocks and pillars, instructing his officials to read his message to those who could not read it themselves.
 
 
 
• Ashoka also sent messengers to spread ideas about dhamma to other lands, such as Syria, Egypt, Greece and Sri Lanka. 
 
• He built roads, dug wells, and built rest houses. Besides, he arranged for medical treatment for both human beings and animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Brihadratha
 
 
• The last ruler of the Maurya Empire.
 
• Assassinated by his general, Pushyamitra Shunga, marking the end of the Maurya dynasty.
 
 
 
• Dasharatha
 
 
• A successor of Ashoka and his grandson, who ruled a smaller part of the Maurya Empire.
 
• Known for issuing minor rock edicts in areas like Nagarjuni and Barabar caves.
 
 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya
 
 
• The founder of the Maurya Empire, uniting most of the Indian subcontinent under one rule.
 
• Mentored by Chanakya (Kautilya), who played a key role in his rise to power.

questions.question: The ministers in the state hold office during the pleasure of the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Governor**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ministers in a state hold office during the pleasure of the **Governor**.
 
• However, this is largely a constitutional formality, as the Governor acts on the advice of the **Chief Minister**.
 
• **The Governor is the constitutional head of the state**, and ministers officially hold office as long as the Governor allows them to
 
• This means that while the** Governor formally appoints ministers and can technically remove them, this is done on the recommendation of the Chief Minister.**
 
• Thus, the phrase “holding office during the pleasure of the Governor” signifies that the real power lies with the elected government, not the Governor

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Deputy Chief Minister**:

 
 
• The Deputy Chief Minister is not a constitutional position and depends on the state's political structure.
 
• While a Deputy Chief Minister may assist the Chief Minister, they do not have the authority to remove ministers.
 
• Their role is more political than constitutional.
 
 
 
• **Speaker of the Legislative Assembly**:
 
 
• The Speaker is responsible for maintaining order in the state legislative assembly and ensuring the smooth functioning of proceedings.
 
• The Speaker's role is confined to legislative matters.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**:
 
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the state government and exercises significant influence in appointing and removing ministers.
 
• Though ministers hold office "during the pleasure of the Governor," the Chief Minister has the actual power to recommend appointments and dismissals.

questions.question: AIDS is an abbreviation for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• AIDS stands for **Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome**.
 
• ** breakdown of the term**:
 
 
• **Acquired**: It is not something you inherit; you get it after birth.
 
• **Immune**: It affects the immune system, which is the body's defense system against infections.
 
• **Deficiency**: It leads to a weakening of the immune system.
 
• **Syndrome**: AIDS is a collection of symptoms and infections resulting from the immune system being damaged.
 
 
 
• AIDS is caused by the **HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus)**,
 
 
• which gradually destroys the immune system, making the body more susceptible to infections and diseases.

questions.question: In which of the following festivals is Kolam drawn?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pongal.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kolam is drawn during many festivals, including Pongal, Deepavali, and Christmas**
 
• **Pongal is a four-day festival **that celebrates the harvest with music, dance, and gift-giving.
 
• During Pongal, families and friends draw colorful and intricate kolam designs outside their homes to attract good vibes and blessings from the gods and goddesses
 
• Kolam **is a centuries-old tradition that originated in ancient Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is a geometrical line drawing made with dots, curves, and loops, and is often drawn around a grid pattern.
 
• **Kolam is a ritual art that is believed to invite positive energy and ward off negativity.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Karma**:

 
 
• This is an agricultural festival celebrated in various parts of India, particularly in the states of Jharkhand, Bihar, and Odisha.
 
• It marks the beginning of the harvest season and involves rituals to honor the deities and seek blessings for a good harvest.
 
• People celebrate by singing, dancing, and performing rituals.
 
 
 
• **Bhogali Bihu:**
 
 
• Also known as Magh Bihu, this is a harvest festival celebrated in Assam, India.
 
• It marks the end of the harvest season and is celebrated in January.
 
• The festival includes feasting, traditional games, and the lighting of bonfires.
 
• People prepare various traditional foods, and community gatherings are a significant part of the celebration.
 
 
 
• **Hareli**:
 
 
• This festival is celebrated in the state of Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is observed during the rainy season and is dedicated to the agricultural deities.
 
• People worship their tools and cattle, symbolizing the importance of agriculture in their lives.
 
• Hareli involves various rituals, traditional songs, and dances.

questions.question: The Vikramshila University was founded under the patronage of the king ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmpala.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dharmapala founded the famous Buddhist monastery at Vikramashila. It became eminent as Nalanda.
 
• Dharmapala became ruler after Gopala in about A.D. 780. He undertook the expansion of his empire.
 
 
• Dharmapala defeated Indrayudha, the king of Kanauj, and installed his nominee Chakrayudha to the throne of Kanauj.
 
• Rashtrakuta king, Dhruva defeated Dharmapala near Monghyr (Bihar) in a battle.
 
 
 
• He was the real founder of the Pala Dynasty because he extensively expanded the boundaries of his empire, and made the Palas a dominant power in northern and eastern India.
 
• He was the 2nd ruler of the Pala dynasty.
 
• He built the great Vihara at Somapuri in Verendri and the Vihara in Paharpur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• After Dharmapala, his son Devapala became the ruler. He was the mightiest Pala king.

 
 
• He conquered – Pragjotishpur (Assam) and Utkala (Odisha).
 
• He patronized the Vikramashila University and Nalanda University.
 
• Famous poet Vajradatta who was the author of Lokesvarashataka was one of the gems of his court.
 
• After the death of Devapala ended the period of ascendancy and a period of stagnation followed which gradually led to decline and disintegration until Mahipala rejuvenated the rule of the dynasty.

questions.question: What is the percentage of people below the poverty line in India according to Government of India, planning commission 2013?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21.92%**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the Government of India's Planning Commission, 21.9%** of India's population lived below the poverty line in 2011-12:

 
 
• Rural areas: 25.7% of the population lived below the poverty line
 
• Urban areas: 13.7% of the population lived below the poverty line 
 
 
 
• Th**e Planning Commission released this data in July 2013,** and it was based on the Tendulkar methodology.
 
• The poverty rate in India decreased from 37.2% in 2004-05 to 21.9% in 2011-12, a decline of 2.18% per year

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Committee calculated poverty levels for the year 2004- 05.
 
• Poverty levels for subsequent years were calculated on the basis of the same methodology, after adjusting for the difference in prices due to inflation.

 
 

 
 
 Kelkar Committee

 
 
 
 It was set up to evaluate and study the PPP (Public-Private Partnership) model in India.

 
 
 

 
 
 Desai Committee

 
 
 
 It was set up to examine the Specific Relief Act,1963

 
 
 

 
 
 Tendulkar Committee

 
 
 
 It was set up to look into the people who were living below the poverty line in India

questions.question: Through an Act passed in which year was the post of Governor-General removed and a new post of Viceroy got created during British rule in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 1858**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• By the Government of India Act 1858, Governor General received the title of Viceroy.
 
• He represented Secretary of State and was assisted by an Executive Council, which consisted of high officials of the Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's rule came directly under British Crown.
 
• The administration was to be run by Her Majesty, through the Secretary of State for India, assisted by the Council of India
 
• The court of Directors and Board of control were abolished.
 
• The council of India was an advisory body, with the secretary of state as its Chairman.
 
• This act made India a direct colony of the British Crown.
 
• Council of India had 15 members, 8 appointed by the Crown and 7 elected by the Court of Directors.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is INCORRECT?

In order to become a member of Vidhan Sabha, a person must:

options.text: have his/her name in the voters’ list
have attained the age of 21 years
not hold any office of profit

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**have attained the age of 21 years**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct age to become a member of the Vidhan Sabha is **25 years**. 
 
• Therefore, option 2 is incorrect
 
• **Eligibility Criteria for Membership of Vidhan Sabha**
 
 
• ​A candidate must have their name included in the **voters’ list** of the state from which they wish to contest.
 
 
• This ensures that the candidate is eligible to vote and represents a constituency where they are recognized as a voter
 
 
 
• The candidate must be a **citizen of India**.
 
 
• This is a basic requirement for all political offices in India, ensuring that only Indian citizens can represent the interests of the people.
 
 
 
• A candidate must not hold any **office of profit** under the government.
 
 
• This means that if someone is currently holding a government job or position that provides a salary or benefits, 
 
 
• they cannot contest elections for the Vidhan Sabha.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Vidhan Sabha**

 
 
• The Vidhan Sabha is the lower house of the state legislature in India.
 
• Each state has its own Vidhan Sabha, and the number of members varies from state to state, typically ranging from 60 to 500 members.
 
• Members are elected directly by the people of the state through a system of universal adult franchise.
 
• The Vidhan Sabha has the power to make laws on various subjects enumerated in the State List and Concurrent List of the Constitution.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the legislative process by discussing, amending, and passing bills. 
 
• Members of the Vidhan Sabha are elected for a term of **five years**

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under the Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Artificial Habits**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Artificial Habitats**:

 
 
• **This topic is not explicitly mentioned in the Concurrent List.**
 
• **It generally pertains to environmental management and conservation measures, w**hich are primarily under the jurisdiction of the states.
 
• The** Indian Constitution divides legislative powers between the Centre and the States** through three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• The **Concurrent List** contains subjects on which both the **Centre and the States** can legislate.
 
• However, in case of any conflict, the law made by the **Central Government** prevails over the State law.
 
• This list contains areas of common interest where a unified legal framework might be beneficial, such as education, marriage laws, and social security.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medical Education**:

 
 
• This falls under the Concurrent List, allowing both the Centre and the states to legislate on this subject.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Wildlife**:
 
 
• This is also included in the Concurrent List, allowing both the central and state governments to take measures regarding wildlife protection.
 
 
 
• **Population Control**:
 
 
• This is part of the Concurrent List, where both levels of government can work together on policies and programs related to population management.

questions.question: A _________ is one billionth of a metre.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** nanometre**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **nanometre** is one billionth of a metre.
 
• It is often abbreviated as **nm** and is commonly used in fields such as physics, chemistry, and nanotechnology to measure extremely small lengths.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• **P​__****arsec** 

 
 
• A parsec (abbreviated as **pc**) is a unit of distance used in astronomy.
 
• It is equivalent to approximately **3.26 light-years** or about **3.09 × 10^16 metres**.
 
• Parsec is used to measure large distances to astronomical objects outside our solar system, such as stars and galaxies.
 
• The term is derived from "parallax" and "arcsecond," reflecting how distances are determined using parallax measurements.
 
 
 
• ** Micrometre**
 
 
• A micrometre (abbreviated as µm) is a unit of length equal to one millionth of a metre (1 µm = 10^-6 m).
 
• Micrometres are commonly used in various scientific fields, including biology (to measure cells and microorganisms), materials science, and engineering.
 
• For instance, the diameter of a human hair is about 70 to 100 micrometres.
 
 
 
• **Angstrom**
 
 
• An angstrom (abbreviated as Å) is a unit of length equal to one ten-billionth of a metre (1 Å = 10^-10 m) or 0.1 nanometres.
 
• Angstroms are primarily used in physics, chemistry, and materials science to measure atomic and molecular scales, such as the wavelengths of light and the sizes of atoms.
 
• For example, the bond length between atoms in a molecule is typically measured in angstroms.

questions.question: ________ is the study of the distribution and movement of water both on and below the Earth’s surface, as well as the impact of human activity on water availability and conditions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Hydrology**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hydrology:
 
 
• Hydrology is the study of the distribution and movement of water both on and below the Earth’s surface, as well as the impact of human activity on water availability and conditions.
 
• It's a scientific discipline in the field of physical geography that also covers the water cycle, water resources, and drainage basin sustainability
 
• Hydrologists are scientists who use scientific techniques and analytical methods to collect and analyze data to help solve water-related problems.
 
 
 
• **Their work can inform policy, planning, and environmental engineering. **
 
• Hydrology is divided into several domains, including:
 
 
• Water quality 
 
• Drainage-basin management
 
• Surface hydrology
 
• Hydrometeorology
 
• Marine hydrology
 
• Groundwater hydrology (hydrogeology)
 
• Surface water hydrology
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biology** ​

 
 
• Biology is the scientific study of life and living organisms.
 
• It encompasses various aspects of life, including structure, function, growth, evolution, distribution, and taxonomy of living organisms.
 
 
• Branches: Some major branches of biology include:
 
• Zoology: Study of animals.
 
• Botany: Study of plants.
 
• Microbiology: Study of microorganisms.
 
• Genetics: Study of heredity and variation in organisms.
 
• Molecular Biology: Study of biological processes at the molecular level.B
 
 
 
 
 
• ** Anthology**
 
 
• An anthology is a collection of literary works, such as poems, short stories, essays, or plays, typically compiled around a common theme or by a specific author or time period.
 
• Types:
 
 
• Poetry Anthology: A collection of poems by various poets or a single poet.
 
• Short Story Anthology: A compilation of short stories, often by multiple authors.
 
• Thematic Anthology: Works grouped by a common theme, such as love, nature, or war.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Ecology**
 
 
• Ecology is the branch of biology that studies the relationships between living organisms and their environment.
 
• It focuses on how organisms interact with each other and with their physical surroundings.
 
• Subfields:
 
 
• Population Ecology: Study of populations of organisms and their interactions with the environment.
 
• Community Ecology: Study of interactions between different species within a community.
 
• Ecosystem Ecology: Study of the flow of energy and materials through ecosystems.
 
• Conservation Ecology: Focus on the preservation and restoration of ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the first population census conducted non-synchronously in different parts of India?

• The first non-synchronous census in India was conducted in 1872.
 
• This census was conducted under the British Raj and covered only British India, excluding princely states.

• The census was significant as it provided valuable insights into the demographics of India and helped in the implementation of policies by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The census is conducted every 10 years in India and the last census was conducted in 2011.
 
• The next census is scheduled to be conducted in 2021.

questions.question: Which is the deepest point of Earth's oceans with a depth of 11,022 metres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Pacific Ocean's Mariana Trench**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mariana Trench, which is the deepest point on earth, is located in the Pacific Ocean.
 
• It is situated in the western Pacific Ocean, to the east of the Mariana Islands.
 
• The Mariana Trench is approximately 2,550 km long and 69 km wide, with a depth of 10,994 meters at its deepest point, known as the Challenger Deep.
 
• The trench is formed by the collision of the Pacific Plate and the Philippine Plate, which creates a subduction zone and leads to the formation of the deepest part of the ocean floor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Atlantic Ocean -

 
 
• This is incorrect because the Atlantic Ocean, while vast and home to significant depths, does not contain the deepest point on Earth.
 
• Its deepest point is the Milwaukee Deep (Puerto Rico Trench), which is approximately 8,376 meters (27,480 feet) deep, far shallower compared to the Mariana Trench.
 
 
 
• Indian Ocean -
 
 
• This option is not correct. The Indian Ocean's deepest point is the Java Trench (also known as the Sunda Trench), with a maximum depth of about 7,725 meters (25,344 feet), making it much shallower than the Mariana Trench.
 
 
 
• Arctic Ocean -
 
 
• This is also incorrect. The Arctic Ocean's deepest point is the Molloy Deep in the Fram Strait, with a depth of about 5,550 meters (18,209 feet).
 
• While fascinating for its own ecological and geographical characteristics, it does not compare to the depth of the Mariana Trench.
 
 

Thus, the Mariana Trench's extreme depth and unique ecosystem have made it a subject of much scientific research and interest, emphasizing its significance located in the Pacific Ocean.
